title: How a waitlist signup becomes a weekly email
subtitle: tiny-waitlist-app, from the signup form to the Monday digest

lanes.label: App server
lanes.sub: API routes, one run per request

nodes.label: /api/signup
nodes.note: skips emails already on the list

nodes.label: /api/confirm
nodes.detail: runs when the link is clicked

steps.text: The visitor types an email and hits Join. The browser sends it to /api/signup.
The server saves the email as 'pending' with a one-time token. If the email is already there, it stops here.
The server asks the email provider to send a confirm link. If that fails it is only logged, so the visitor waits for an email that never comes.
The visitor clicks the link in their inbox. Only some people do.
The link opens /api/confirm with the token.
Every Monday at 09:00 the job reads the last 7 days of posts. No posts means no email that week.
One model call turns those posts into a short digest.
The job loads every confirmed subscriber.
It sends the digest to each one: one paid email per person.

takeaways: Nobody got a confirm email? Check the server log for 'confirm email failed'. The signup still looks fine to the visitor.
No digest on Monday? First check DIGEST_ENABLED, then whether any posts were written that week.
Costs grow with the list: one model call a week, but one paid email per confirmed person.
Pending rows never expire: no code in this app cleans them up.
